courses.name: Calculus I
courses.description: Introduces single-variable derivatives, limits, continuity, approximation and optimization.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Algebra, trigonometry and analytic geometry. Although the course will make use of computers, no programming experience is assumed.; Credit limitation: Credit may not be earned for both MA1021 and MA1020.

category_review.rationale: Differential calculus methods define the subject.

courses.name: Calculus II
courses.description: Develops integration, its foundational theorem, computational techniques and geometric or engineering applications.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): MA 1020 or MA 1021 . Although the course will make use of computers, no programming experience is assumed.

category_review.rationale: Integral calculus remains central despite engineering examples.

courses.name: Matrices and Linear Algebra I
courses.description: Introduces matrices, linear equations, transformations, eigenvalues, vector spaces and numerical linear-algebra methods.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): None, although basic knowledge of equations for planes and lines in space would be helpful.; Credit limitation: Credit may not be earned for both MA2071 and MA2072.

category_review.rationale: The description explicitly develops linear-algebra theory and techniques.

courses.name: Accelerated Matrices and Linear Algebra I
courses.description: Accelerates linear algebra through vector spaces, eigenvalues, least squares and singular-value methods, with computational examples.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Basic knowledge of matrix algebra; Credit limitation: Credit may not be earned for both MA2072 and MA2071.

category_review.rationale: Matrix and vector-space theory organize the data-science applications.

courses.name: Matrices and Linear Algebra II
courses.description: Deepens linear algebra through abstract spaces, transformations, polynomials, diagonalization and matrix exponentials.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): MA 2071 or MA 2072 .

category_review.rationale: Advanced linear-algebra theory is explicit.

courses.name: Applied Statistics I
courses.description: Introduces applied statistical analysis through study design, data exploration, estimation and hypothesis tests using real datasets and software.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): MA 1022 .

category_review.rationale: Statistical inference and study design are the central methods, despite practical industrial/scientific examples.

courses.name: Applied Statistics II
courses.description: Continues applied statistics with regression, categorical-data tables, experimental analysis and distribution-free methods.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): MA 2611 .

category_review.rationale: The complete description develops statistical methods rather than an unspecified data-science survey.

courses.name: Introduction to Programming for Non-Majors
courses.description: Introduces imperative and scripting programs, control flow, decomposition, basic structures, testing and data/device interfaces.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): None. All Computer Science students and other students wishing to prepare for 3000-level courses in Computer Science should take CS 1101 / CS 1102 instead of CS 1004 . This course provides sufficient background for CS 2301 Systems Programming for Non-Majors.

category_review.rationale: Programming construction and debugging are central.

courses.name: Introduction to Program Design
courses.description: Develops functional program design using structured data, recursion, higher-order functions and testing.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): None. Either CS 1101 or CS 1102 provides sufficient background for further courses in the CS department. Undergraduate credit may not be earned for both this course and CS 1102 .

category_review.rationale: General program design and implementation establish foundational computer science.

courses.name: Accelerated Introduction to Program Design
courses.description: Combines accelerated functional programming with selected advanced programming topics and an individual project.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Substantial prior programming experience (including functions, recursion, and lists, as would be covered in high-school Advanced Placement Computer Science A courses, but not necessarily AP CS Principles courses). Either CS 1101 or CS 1102 provides sufficient background for further courses in the CS department. Undergraduate credit may not be earned for both this course and CS 1101 .

category_review.rationale: The entire course remains focused on program construction, despite examples involving web protocols and languages.

courses.name: Leadership Practice
courses.description: Examines leadership through self-awareness, communication, cultural differences, ethics and contemporary organizational challenges.

category_review.rationale: Human relationships, communication and ethical leadership organize the complete description.

courses.name: Financial Statements for Decision Making
courses.description: Uses financial statements, accounting concepts and sensitivity analysis to support business decisions and assess stakeholder impacts.

category_review.rationale: Substantive accounting and financial-statement interpretation are the domain.

courses.name: Risk Analysis for Decision Making
courses.description: Introduces financial decisions through valuation, interest rates, investment risk and returns, establishing financial literacy for further study.

category_review.rationale: The actual description concerns substantive finance and valuation, not generic decision-theory mathematics or AI.

courses.name: Engineering Economics
courses.description: Evaluates engineering alternatives through financial value, cash flow, tax, inflation, uncertainty and replacement decisions.

category_review.rationale: Engineering economics and financial decisions establish applied domain knowledge; arithmetic does not alone imply a mathematics course.

courses.name: Marketing Strategy
courses.description: Develops marketing strategies from customer insights, segmentation, competitive analysis and market conditions.

category_review.rationale: Strategic marketing practice is the dominant domain.

courses.name: Global Environment of Business Decisions
courses.description: Examines global business environments through trade, culture, political risk, financial systems, law and supply chains.

category_review.rationale: The description integrates social/political/cultural analysis with business-domain decisions without a clearly dominant taxonomy subject.

courses.name: The Legal Environment of Business Decisions
courses.description: Examines contracts, torts, intellectual property and organizational law in technology and global business decisions.

category_review.rationale: Legal interpretation is central, despite business examples.

courses.name: Social Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Develops social-enterprise models, opportunity assessment, impact evaluation, organizational structures and financing.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Familiarity with concepts of creativity, innovation, entrepreneurial and critical thinking, ethics, cross-cultural relations, and social problems ( OBC 1010 , BUS 1020 , ACC 2060 or equivalent).

category_review.rationale: Entrepreneurship tools and operation of social ventures organize the social-problem context.

courses.name: Growing and Managing New Ventures
courses.description: Examines how ventures expand markets, plan products, manage operations and sustain cash flow as they grow.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): ACC 2101 , OBC 1010 , BUS 1020 , BUS 2020 , ACC 2060 , MIS 3010 , OIE 3020 , MKT 4030 , ETR 3913, OIE 2850 .

category_review.rationale: New-venture management is substantive business practice.

courses.name: Leadership, Ethics, and Social Responsibility
courses.description: Investigates ethical leadership, corporate governance and social responsibility through reflection and organizational cases.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): None.

category_review.rationale: Ethics and social responsibility are the explicit central subjects.

courses.name: Application Building with Object-Oriented Concepts
courses.description: Develops object-oriented applications through design, implementation and debugging, with interfaces and database access.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Programming experience such as found in CS 1101 , CS 1102 , CS 1004 , or CS 1005 .

category_review.rationale: General software construction and object-oriented programming are the central subject.

courses.name: Data Science I: Introduction to Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Introduces data preparation, programming, statistics, learning methods, visualization and responsible AI through projects with real datasets.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): None

category_review.rationale: The broad introduction deliberately spans programming, mathematical analysis and AI methods without establishing one dominant subject.

courses.name: Data Science II: Statistical Modeling and Analysis
courses.description: Develops prediction and inference workflows with regression, classification, decision trees, dimensionality reduction, feature engineering and bias-variance analysis.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Data science basics equivalent to DS 1010 , applied statistics and regression equivalent to MA 2611 and MA 2612 , and the ability to write computer programs in a scientific language equivalent to a CS programming course at the CS 1000 or CS 2000 level are assumed.

category_review.rationale: After a brief mathematics review, the description explicitly centers introductory machine-learning methods and predictive data workflows.

courses.name: Database Systems I
courses.description: Develops relational databases through models, queries, design theory, data independence and implementation.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): CS 2022 and either CS 2102 , CS 2103 , or CS 2119 .; Credit limitation: Undergraduate credit may not be earned for both CS3431 and CS542.

category_review.rationale: Database systems and storage/design abstractions establish systems content.

courses.name: Big Data Management and Analytics
courses.description: Studies distributed data infrastructure, streaming, cloud platforms, query optimization and scalable analytics through projects.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Knowledge in database systems at the level of CS 4432 , and programming experience are assumed.

category_review.rationale: Distributed database infrastructure, storage and query processing dominate the analytics context.

courses.name: Business Applications of Blockchain
courses.description: Studies blockchain operation, smart contracts, business applications, implementation projects and regulatory challenges.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Basic knowledge of programming (Equivalent to CS 1004 or other introductory programming courses)

category_review.rationale: Computing infrastructure and business application practice both receive explicit attention; neither clearly dominates.

courses.name: Business Data Management
courses.description: Designs and implements business databases using relational models, queries, normalization and concurrency/recovery techniques.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Some programming knowledge (e.g., CS 1004 , CS 2119 , OIE 2600 or equivalent knowledge)

category_review.rationale: The description teaches database mechanisms and design, not merely business use of software.

courses.name: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Develops AI representation, search, planning and language understanding through computational problem-solving projects.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): CS 2102 or CS 2103 ; CS 2223 ; and CS 3133 .; Credit limitation: Undergraduate credit may not be earned for both CS4341 and CS534.

category_review.rationale: Explicit AI methods and search-based problem solving define the course.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence with Business Application
courses.description: Develops AI knowledge representation, search, planning and language understanding through problem-solving projects.

category_review.rationale: The actual description teaches AI methods; the business-oriented title does not reduce it to general business applications.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.description: Explores theoretical and practical learning algorithms for prediction, representation, clustering and probabilistic modeling.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Multivariate Calculus ( MA 1024 or MA 1034 ), Linear Algebra (such as MA 2071 ), Probability ( MA 2621 or MA 2631 ), and Algorithms ( CS 2223 ). Students may not earn credit for both CS 453X and CS 4342 . Undergraduate credit may not be earned both for this course and for CS 539.

category_review.rationale: Machine-learning algorithms are explicit throughout the complete description.

courses.name: Business Applications of Machine Learning
courses.description: Applies supervised and automated machine-learning tools to prediction problems across several business domains.

category_review.rationale: The course explicitly develops machine-learning approaches across varied applications, rather than teaching one business domain alone.

courses.name: Data Analysis for Decision Making
courses.description: Uses business analytics and advanced spreadsheets to support forecasting, operations and customer-related decisions.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Basic statistics, equivalent to that in MA 2611 and MA 2612 .

category_review.rationale: Business decision practice organizes the data techniques; no specific AI-method focus is established.

courses.name: Introduction to Prescriptive Analytics
courses.description: Introduces optimization and simulation for selecting actions across varied engineering and management problems.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Basic statistics, equivalent to that in MA 2611 and MA 2612 .

category_review.rationale: Mathematical optimization and simulation are the transferable central methods across the example domains.

courses.name: Financial Analytics
courses.description: Develops predictive financial-data models using clustering, classification, regression, regularization and validation in R.

category_review.rationale: The stated objective and detailed topics center modern machine-learning methods; financial problems supply the application data.

courses.name: Marketing Analytics
courses.description: Applies marketing analytics to segmentation, churn, pricing and customer value in business cases.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Foundational knowledge in Marketing or Consumer Behavior (equivalent to MKT 1100 or MKT 2640 ) and Knowledge of Statistics (equivalent to that in MA 2611 or MA 2612 ).

category_review.rationale: Marketing decision practice dominates; analytics terminology alone does not establish an AI-method course.

courses.name: Achieving Effective Operations
courses.description: Analyzes and implements operating processes amid resource, stakeholder, sustainability and ethical constraints.

category_review.rationale: Operational process management and practical improvement are the substantive domain.

courses.name: Business Intelligence
courses.description: Uses business-intelligence software and case analysis to turn organizational data into recommendations.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Previous knowledge in data management, such as that provided by MIS 3720 Business Data Management or CS 3431 Database Systems I.

category_review.rationale: Business decision support through existing tools is central, rather than computing infrastructure or explicit AI methods.

courses.name: Marketing Research
courses.description: Develops marketing research from problem formulation through study design, data collection and communication of findings.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Foundational knowledge in Marketing or Consumer Behavior (equivalent to MKT 1100 or MKT 2640 ) and Knowledge of Statistics (equivalent to that in MA 2611 or MA 2612 ).

category_review.rationale: Research methods serve explicit marketing decisions and domain practice.

courses.name: Sales Management and Analytics
courses.description: Combines sales strategy, employee management, negotiation and data analysis to align selling with organizational goals.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Foundational knowledge in Marketing or Consumer Behavior (equivalent to MKT 1100 or MKT 2640 ) + Knowledge of Statistics (equivalent to that in MA 2611 or MA 2612 ).

category_review.rationale: Sales management and professional selling are the primary applied domain.

courses.name: Consumer Behavior and Analytics
courses.description: Uses consumer theories and market data to inform segmentation, branding, pricing and other marketing decisions.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Knowledge of Statistics (equivalent to that in MA 2611 or MA 2612 ).; Credit limitation: Credit may not be earned for both MKT2640 and MKT3650.

category_review.rationale: Psychological and social theories support practical consumer/marketing analysis; the business domain remains dominant.

courses.name: E-Commerce and Web Analytics
courses.description: Uses web-performance measures, search strategies and customer targeting to improve digital-commerce decisions.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Foundational knowledge in Marketing or Consumer Behavior (equivalent to MKT 1100 or MKT 2640 ) and Knowledge of Statistics (equivalent to that in MA 2611 or MA 2612 ).

category_review.rationale: Digital commerce and marketing effectiveness are the practical domain, not systems engineering.

courses.name: Digital and Social Media Marketing Analytics
courses.description: Examines digital-media analytics for marketing mix, branding, communication and customer relationships.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Foundational knowledge in Marketing or Consumer Behavior (equivalent to MKT 1100 or MKT 2640 ) and Knowledge of Statistics (equivalent to that in MA 2611 or MA 2612 ).

category_review.rationale: The course centers marketing management and brand practice rather than general data-science methods.

courses.name: Simulation Modeling and Analysis
courses.description: Develops simulation experiments and statistical interpretation using queueing, inventory and industrial examples.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): CS 1004 and MA 2612 .

category_review.rationale: Simulation methodology, experimental design and statistical analysis organize the domain examples.

courses.name: Stochastic Models
courses.description: Develops risk-based decisions with stochastic models including Markov chains, Poisson processes and queues.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): Knowledge of calculus and introductory probability and statistics.

category_review.rationale: Probability models and quantitative risk methods are the central subject.

courses.name: Advanced Prescriptive Analytics: From Data to Impact
courses.description: Formulates and solves advanced optimization problems with integer variables, nonlinear relationships and uncertainty.
courses.prerequisites: Recommended background (not a mandatory prerequisite): An introductory level of exposure to prescriptive analytics or linear optimization, such as can be found in OIE 2081 , MA 2210 , or MA 3231 .; Suggested background (advisory): Note the mathematical foundations of some of the optimization techniques in this class are in MA 3231 . Students might also benefit from MA 3233 .; Credit limitation: Credit may not be earned for both OIE4430 and OIE4420.

category_review.rationale: Mathematical model formulation and solution methods dominate the varied practical examples.

courses.name: Engineering Innovation and Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Examines commercial aspects of engineering innovation and how new products and ventures develop.

category_review.rationale: Entrepreneurship and commercialization establish the applied business domain.

courses.name: Creating Value Through Innovation
courses.description: Evaluates innovations through customers, organizational capabilities, competitors and ethical or financial value.

category_review.rationale: Innovation assessment and commercialization are substantive business practice.

courses.name: Inquiry Seminar in Humanities and Arts
courses.description: Culminating humanities and arts inquiry develops communication, critical thinking and engagement with diverse perspectives through an instructor-defined theme.
courses.prerequisites: Course eligibility: Before enrollment, complete five Humanities and Arts courses, with at least two thematically related and at least one at the 2000 level or above.

category_review.rationale: The complete description explicitly centers communication, critical inquiry and appreciation of diverse perspectives in humanities/arts; thematic variability does not imply a technical AI subject.

courses.name: Practicum in Humanities and Arts
courses.description: Culminating humanities and arts inquiry develops communication, critical thinking and engagement with diverse perspectives through an instructor-defined theme.
courses.prerequisites: Course eligibility: Before enrollment, complete five Humanities and Arts courses, with at least two thematically related and at least one at the 2000 level or above. Instructor consent is also required.

category_review.rationale: The complete description explicitly centers communication, critical inquiry and appreciation of diverse perspectives in humanities/arts; thematic variability does not imply a technical AI subject.

requirements.summary: 1. BUS 2080 Data Analysis for Decision Making or OIE 2081 Introduction to Prescriptive Analytics

requirements.title: Analytics Foundation slot 2
requirements.summary: 2. FIN 3330 Financial Analytics or MKT 4040 Marketing Analytics

requirements.title: Analytics Foundation slot 3
requirements.summary: 3. OIE 3020 Achieving Effective Operations or other 3000 or higher-level OIE course

requirements.title: Analytics Foundation slot 4
requirements.summary: 4. MIS 4084 Business Intelligence or other 4000-level MIS course

requirements.title: Basic science
requirements.summary: Eligible prefixes: BB, CH, GE, PH. The program page omits quantity; the separately sourced university baseline requires at least 2/3 unit of natural or engineering science.

requirements.title: Six electives across three categories
requirements.summary: Six electives across three categories

requirements.title: Business Analytics Applications (Select at least 3)
requirements.summary: At least three courses in business analytics applications.

requirements.title: Computing Technologies, Data and Mathematical Sciences (Maximum 3)
requirements.summary: At most three: CS3000+ except CS3043; DS/MA2000+; CS2119 or MIS2300.

requirements.title: Business and Entrepreneurship (Maximum 2):
requirements.summary: At most two: previously unused OBC courses, BUS1020/BUS2020, ETR courses, or MIS3010.

requirements.title: Major Qualifying Project
requirements.summary: Required senior capstone supervised by full-time Business School faculty who teach analytics, AI or STEM.

requirements.title: Overlap and double-major restrictions
requirements.summary: Each course fills only one program slot. A simultaneous Marketing Analytics major is prohibited.

requirements.title: Graduate-course substitutions
requirements.summary: WPI limits on graduate credit apply. Admission to a graduate business program must precede graduate business courses; undergraduate versions do not satisfy corresponding graduate requirements.

requirements.title: Transfer after matriculation
requirements.summary: Off-campus study after WPI matriculation needs prior written permission for transferable credit.

requirements.title: Minimum academic credit
requirements.summary: Earn at least 15 academic units; use free electives beyond published distribution requirements to reach the minimum.

requirements.title: Residence
requirements.summary: At least eight units must be completed satisfactorily in residence at WPI.

requirements.title: Humanities and arts
requirements.summary: Two units with the applicable humanities/arts sequence and completion evaluation.

requirements.title: Mathematics and science baseline
requirements.summary: Two units in science, engineering, mathematics or computing, subject to the program’s stricter distribution.

requirements.title: Quantitative science baseline
requirements.summary: At least 2/3 unit in quantitative science; eligible subjects are determined by the major.

requirements.title: Natural or engineering science baseline
requirements.summary: At least 2/3 unit in natural or engineering science; the major determines eligible subjects.

requirements.title: Remaining science baseline
requirements.summary: The remaining 2/3 unit may be quantitative, natural or engineering science.

requirements.title: Interactive Qualifying Project
requirements.summary: At least one unit of an approved project relating science/technology to society, with required documentation.

requirements.title: Major Qualifying Project
requirements.summary: At least one unit of an approved project in the major, with required documentation. This includes rather than adds to the program MQP.

requirements.title: Program distribution certification
requirements.summary: Complete the major’s published distribution; certification is by its Program Review Committee on adviser recommendation.

requirements.title: Social sciences
requirements.summary: At least 2/3 social-science unit, excluding qualifying-project work.

requirements.title: Wellness and physical education
requirements.summary: Complete 1/3 WPE unit (normally four classes) or an approved equivalent.

requirements.title: Standard humanities sequence
requirements.summary: Complete five HUA courses before HU3900/HU3910 or an equivalent 1/3-unit inquiry seminar/practicum; submit the completion form afterward.

requirements.title: Thematic depth
requirements.summary: Before the capstone, take at least three related courses in AR, MU, TH, EN/WR/RH, HI/HU/INTL, PY/RE, or a faculty-approved interdisciplinary theme.

requirements.title: Depth level
requirements.summary: At least one depth course preceding the capstone must be at 2000 level or above. A 3000-level course is encouraged, not required.

requirements.title: Breadth outside depth area
requirements.summary: Before the capstone, take a course outside the depth grouping. Groups: AR/TH/MU; SP/GN/ISE/AB/CN; EN/WR/RH; HI/HU/INTL; PY/RE. Six-course modern-language sequences are exempt.

requirements.title: Language alternatives
requirements.summary: Language paths: a practicum as the sixth language course; an advanced seminar after five language courses; or advanced-placement language competence with a mixed approved sequence ending in an advanced seminar.

requirements.title: Non-native English path
requirements.summary: Non-native English speakers may combine ISE/WR work and conclude with a project-based ISE/WR course at 3000 level or above.

requirements.title: Practicum permission
requirements.summary: Instructor permission is required for the practicum.

requirements.title: Advanced placement ceiling
requirements.summary: At most 1/3 AP unit counts toward HUA. German/Spanish scores 4–5 qualify subject to the starting-course restriction; studio art requires portfolio review. Additional AP credit may satisfy other requirements.

requirements.title: Transfer completion alternatives
requirements.summary: Transfers with fewer than six HUA courses complete the remaining two-unit sequence including a capstone. Two units completed before entry may satisfy HUA through coordinator approval of the completion form.

requirements.title: Transfer-credit evaluation
requirements.summary: The general HUA rule accepts accredited US courses at B- or better; non-US work is individually reviewed. Prior approval is required after matriculation. The language subsection also retains legacy B/C thresholds and recommends B-; obtain coordinator determination for that conflict.

requirements.title: Prior language study
requirements.summary: Without AP, three years of high-school language may yield 1/3 transfer unit after two WPI courses at intermediate level or above. AP/high-school pathways require starting WPI language study at Elementary II or above.

requirements.title: Off-campus humanities alternative
requirements.summary: An approved HUA project-center term may combine with at least three prior HUA courses/equivalents. HUA admission, required forms, adviser-directed preparation, written report and any required presentation apply; normally finish within one term under HUA faculty supervision.

requirements.title: Eligible social sciences
requirements.summary: Two SSPS courses qualify: ECON, ENV, DEV, GOV, PSY, SD, SOC, SS or STS. SS/ID2050 qualifies. A 1/3-unit Great Problems Seminar may qualify only with a co-teacher holding at least a half-time SSPS appointment.

requirements.title: Social science exclusions
requirements.summary: HUA, Business School and STEM social-implications courses do not qualify; CS3043/SS3043, IMGD2000 and EDU4100 are specifically excluded.

requirements.title: Social-science overlap
requirements.summary: Eligible social-science courses may also satisfy major distribution requirements.

requirements.title: Wellness alternatives and approval
requirements.summary: Repeated WPE courses may earn credit; independent study is unavailable. Approved varsity/club participation requires advance registration (varsity instructor permission); approved off-campus courses require advance approval. No retroactive credit. Some ROTC participation qualifies after commander review.

requirements.title: IQP preparation
requirements.summary: Global Projects Program IQPs require a preparation course before travel. Projects may be on or off campus; reports are archived in Digital WPI.

requirements.title: MQP disciplinary context
requirements.summary: The MQP applies disciplinary knowledge to a representative professional problem, selected with the adviser to complement the overall program. A preliminary proposal is encouraged, not universally required.

requirements.title: Credit-bearing completion
requirements.summary: A/B/C are undergraduate course grades that earn credit; NR does not. IQP/MQP/HUA require an overall completion evaluation; project SP is temporary and must be replaced by a permanent grade.

requirements.title: No institutional undergraduate GPA
requirements.summary: WPI does not maintain an undergraduate cumulative GPA. A numerical equivalent may be requested for external use; no GPA graduation threshold is inferred.

requirements.title: Major certification
requirements.summary: The appropriate program review committee certifies the major using the completed distribution and MQP, in consultation with the student and adviser.

requirements.title: Optional double-major rules
requirements.summary: Complete both distributions and one MQP unit in each major plus one IQP unit (three project units). Appropriate shared academic work may satisfy both majors; program-review approvals apply. The more detailed Degree Options policy also permits approved interdisciplinary MQP and social-science exceptions.

requirements.title: Graduate-course use and conversion
requirements.summary: Graduate enrollment ordinarily does not require graduate admission; Business School courses require admission to a dual BS/MS program. The published conversion is one graduate credit to 1/6 undergraduate unit, processed by the Registrar.

requirements.title: Optional combined-degree approval
requirements.summary: Shared BS/MS coursework requires adviser/graduate-coordinator planning and an approved course-selection agreement submitted to the Registrar. The agreement never waives either degree’s requirements.

requirements.title: Optional BS/MS shared-credit limit
requirements.summary: Shared credit cannot exceed 40% of the master degree’s required credits; some departments limit it to 30%. The chosen graduate program and approved agreement determine the actual allowance.

requirements.title: Concentration declaration and scope
requirements.summary: A concentration requires two integrated-study units and a related MQP. Plan with the adviser and apply to the program review committee by its deadlines; concentration requirements cannot prevent completion of the major.

requirements.title: Additional-designation overlap ceiling
requirements.summary: Concentrations/minors may overlap another additional designation by at most one unit. No credit-bearing activity may be triple-counted across degree requirements or designations.

requirements.title: Double-major eligibility
requirements.summary: At most two undergraduate majors; both programs must permit the combination. Exceptions to prohibited combinations need Committee on Academic Operations approval.

requirements.title: Interdisciplinary double-major MQP alternative
requirements.summary: With advance signed approval, a 4/3-unit interdisciplinary MQP may satisfy both majors instead of two one-unit MQPs. It must cover both fields and be advised by faculty associated with both. Both program audits require certification; HUA is unchanged.

requirements.title: Social-science double-major exception
requirements.summary: A social-science MQP may also satisfy IQP when an approved one-unit project meets both sets of goals. An interdisciplinary double-major MQP cannot also be the IQP.

requirements.title: Disallowed business double majors
requirements.summary: Cannot combine this degree with Business, Financial Technology, Information Systems and Technology, Management Engineering, Marketing Analytics, except with Committee on Academic Operations approval.

requirements.title: Degree application deadline
requirements.summary: Apply to the Registrar for May graduation during the preceding A term; for September or December graduation during the preceding D term.

requirements.title: Transfer-credit approval
requirements.summary: Departments evaluate comparable accredited-institution courses individually. Normally C or better is considered; departments may require B- or higher. Vocational, correspondence, precollege/review, CEU, enrichment/refresher and CLEP work is excluded.

requirements.title: Approval before outside study
requirements.summary: After matriculation, obtain department approval and its specified minimum grade on the transfer authorization form, file before study, then submit an official transcript. Consortium work may need separate distribution approval; otherwise it may be elective credit.

requirements.title: Retroactive language credit conditions
requirements.summary: Without AP, retroactive language credit requires three high-school years averaging B, placement at least into term two, and two qualifying WPI terms graded B or better. Spanish specifically requires SP2521/2522. AP and high-school pathways cannot both earn credit.

requirements.title: Retroactive calculus credit conditions
requirements.summary: Retroactive MA1021/1022 credit follows the specified sequential WPI calculus/MA2051 pathways. Both qualifying courses must pass on first attempt by D term of year one, with no first-year NR in MA1021–1024.

requirements.title: AP and other prior-learning credit
requirements.summary: AP/IB/PLTW awards depend on the applicable examination, score and department equivalency policy. They are credit-award alternatives, not a waiver of the degree distribution. HUA AP is capped at 1/3 unit.

requirements.title: Project approval and registration
requirements.summary: An adviser must accept the project before registration. Register by the first term of work; no-penalty registration closes on term day ten. MQP supervision must include faculty associated with the major.

requirements.title: Project reporting
requirements.summary: Meet adviser expectations for interim work and a satisfactory final report. Sponsor projects normally need written/oral reports; team documentation must identify individual contributions.

requirements.title: Electronic project submission
requirements.summary: Submit the final IQP/MQP as PDF electronically with adviser approval, normally one report per team; register for at least 1/6 project unit in the submission term.

requirements.title: Degree-requirement completion recording
requirements.summary: Completion forms are due by day ten of the following term; May candidates need the eCDR by the last Thursday of D term. After day ten, recording MQP/IQP/HUA completion requires at least 1/6 unit of that activity in the current term unless a written adviser petition is approved.

requirements.title: Sponsor review and agreements
requirements.summary: Off-campus work requires proper registration and sponsor-agreement compliance. Submit sponsor copies early for confidentiality review (often 30 days); final grading/submission waits for that review.

requirements.title: Global-project overload restriction
requirements.summary: No overload during a one-term off-campus Global Projects Program project or the preceding ID2050-plus-prequalifying-project term.

requirements.title: Paid sponsored-project conditions
requirements.summary: Paid IQP/MQP work needs Undergraduate Studies approval before work: documented learning purpose, faculty control of assessment, and approved project agreement/scope. Submit by day five of the preceding term and remain registered during work; prior unregistered employment earns no project credit.

requirements.title: Fall Semester degree application
requirements.summary: Current registrar table: apply by October 4th for fall semester completion and December degree conferral. The catalog separately gives prior-term timing and a September conferral reference; that source discrepancy is preserved for review.

requirements.title: Spring Semester degree application
requirements.summary: Current registrar table: apply by October 4 th for spring semester completion and May degree conferral. The catalog separately gives prior-term timing and a September conferral reference; that source discrepancy is preserved for review.

requirements.title: Summer Semester degree application
requirements.summary: Current registrar table: apply by July 15th for summer semester completion and August degree conferral. The catalog separately gives prior-term timing and a September conferral reference; that source discrepancy is preserved for review.

requirements.title: Optional Business School BS/MS eligibility
requirements.summary: Business graduate courses require prior graduate-program admission. Only graduate credits may be shared with a Business School MS; undergraduate courses cannot count toward it. MBA and MS Financial Technology are excluded from this BS/MS option. Business applications are first reviewed after sophomore C term. This FAQ supplies no universal undergraduate graduate-course count cap; the approved plan and existing shared-credit limits still govern.
